renderPacket.identity: One real photographically recognizable view looking south from Timothy Hill Overlook, Southeast Peninsula, St. Kitts: narrow green volcanic peninsula, Atlantic Ocean on the left/east, Caribbean Sea on the right/west, real gently winding road along the peninsula and distinctive conical Nevis Peak rising beyond the Narrows. Quiet natural daylight; preserve actual island silhouette, local topography, shorelines and road alignment. Broad horizontal Hero with clear central subject and safe mobile crop; restrained 60% photographic realism and 40% delicate watercolor texture. No invented buildings, coastline or roads.

Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park on northwest St. Kitts. One authentic close panoramic view of the actual low dark basalt Fort George citadel battlements and angular bastions around grassy parade ground atop a steep lush volcanic hill, Caribbean Sea and distant island horizon. Preserve the citadel's polygonal real-world stone geometry and limestone arch details; no castles, towers or imaginary walls. Quiet warm daylight; recognizable landscape in subtle, elegant naturalistic watercolor with genuine photographic structure; horizontal image, distinct from approved Timothy Hill peninsula Hero.

Mount Liamuiga summit CRATER in northern St. Kitts, NOT a coast: an inward-facing near-field image from a jagged forested crater lip into a 1-km-wide enclosed steep-walled bowl densely filled with genuine tropical green rainforest and ferns, patches of mist trapped within. All the image is land and volcanic crater; neither ocean nor peninsula nor coastal roads nor distant island silhouettes appear. Real world jagged rim and forested interior of Liamuiga documented by the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program. Delicate naturalistic watercolor on faithful terrain; single landscape, no text, no collage, entirely different visual composition from the approved coastal Hero.

BLACK ROCKS lava outcrop at Belle Vue on the exposed northeastern Atlantic coast of ST. KITTS, from the shore-level viewpoint. Black, jagged rough volcanic basalt pillars, boulders and cooled lava occupy MOST OF THE FRAME; white surf breaks directly over and between the dark black stone. Thin edge of low green grass and a flat open sea horizon; no sandy beach, bay, yachts, pier, mountain, village, palm trees or peninsula. A geologically recognizable one-place image, naturalistic delicate watercolor over faithfully observed dark rock formations. ONE standalone scene without text, panels or reused coast panorama.

Documentary accurate street-level view of Independence Square in Basseterre, St. Kitts: shaded urban green square, authentic surrounding modest two-storey colonial Caribbean storefronts and recognizably proportioned pale St. George's Anglican Church on its actual edge, local pedestrian-scale streets. Subtle everyday human presence, no invented high-rises or exaggerated cathedral, not a generic European plaza. Quiet naturalistic watercolor with identifiable built heritage, distinctly urban.

Romney Manor / Caribelle Batik garden in western St. Kitts. Real grand centuries-old spreading saman tree, shady tropical garden, low historic stone estate structures, modest authentic outdoor batik workshop glimpsed without text or invented displays. Convey the relation between plantation-era grounds and living textile craft in calm daylight. Single photorealistically grounded restrained watercolor scene, no postcard collage and no fantasy mansion.

Nevis Peak on Nevis island seen from a real lower volcanic slope with lush forest and scattered low cloud around its broad conical upper profile. Focus landward on steep green volcanic mountain with natural forest textures, not the narrow St. Kitts peninsula or two-seas panorama; accurately represent single Nevis volcanic cone without invented lakes or dramatic lava. Quiet natural daylight, subtle watercolor over recognizable terrain, horizontal single frame.

Authentic Charlestown waterfront street on western Nevis: low-rise historical Caribbean stone and timber buildings, modest small shops, a short real harbor-side lane and quiet local daily life with small inter-island ferry context. A documentary street-height perspective, genuine Nevis scale, not Basseterre Independence Square, no ornate fabricated colonial palace and no readable signage or letters. Calm soft-daylight delicate watercolor over faithfully observed architecture.

Real Pinney's Beach on the western Caribbean-facing shore of Nevis. Long naturally curving broad sand beach, a few authentic leaning coconut palms, transparent calm water, on the far horizon the actual green mountainous silhouette of St. Kitts across the Narrows. Modest unobtrusive local beach hut only if geographically plausible, no overwater villas or manufactured resort setting; warm subdued daylight and airy naturalistic watercolor, no repetition of the Timothy Hill elevated panorama.
